info.title: automaton
info.description: Automaton CLI — deploy apps, manage runners, publish versions

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Automaton CLI — create, deploy, and publish Automaton apps

commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a new Automaton app and link this directory

commands.name: sync-ai
commands.description: Refresh the generated local AI guidance files in this folder

options.name: --adapter
options.description: Optional AI tool adapter to generate: none, claude, copilot, github-skills, or all

commands.name: login
commands.description: Store CLI credentials and validate them against the server

options.name: --global
options.description: Store credentials in ~/.automaton/config.json instead of the current project

commands.name: logout
commands.description: Clear stored CLI credentials

options.name: --all
options.description: Clear both project-local and global stored credentials

commands.name: whoami
commands.description: Show the current authenticated Automaton user

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create a remote Automaton app for the current folder and write appId into automaton.json

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show the current linked app, deploy settings, and publish state

commands.name: current-runner
commands.description: Show the runner currently assigned to the linked app

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Validate the current project before deploy or publish

options.name: --non-interactive
options.description: Disable rich terminal rendering and use plain output

commands.name: init
commands.description: Create a new Automaton app or link an existing one to this directory

options.name: --app
options.description: Link to an existing app ID instead of creating a new one

options.name: --name
options.description: App name (required when creating a new app)

commands.name: link
commands.description: Link this directory to an existing Automaton app

arguments.name: APP_ID
arguments.description: Existing Automaton app ID to link to this directory

commands.name: deploy
commands.description: Build, upload, and deploy the app to Automaton

options.name: --runner
options.description: Runner ID or exact runner name to assign before backend deploy when needed

options.name: --clean
options.description: Wipe all server-side app files before uploading (full replace)

options.name: --skip-backend
options.description: Skip deploying backend Python scripts after upload

options.name: --dir
options.description: Frontend directory to upload (overrides frontend.deployDir in automaton.json)

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Print ignored-file details and exclusion reasons

options.name: --publish
options.description: Publish the app after a successful deploy

options.name: --open
options.description: Open the deployed app in the browser after success

options.name: --non-interactive
options.description: Disable prompts and rich terminal rendering

commands.name: open
commands.description: Open the current app in the browser

options.name: --public
options.description: Open the published public app URL

options.name: --private
options.description: Open the private deployed app URL

commands.name: pull
commands.description: Download editable app source files from the server

options.name: --dir
options.description: Target directory (defaults to current directory for refresh mode, or a new subfolder in the current directory for app mode)

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite matching local files without prompting

options.name: --non-interactive
options.description: Disable progress rendering and use plain output

arguments.name: APP
arguments.description: App ID or slug to pull into a new local folder

commands.name: publish
commands.description: Make the latest deployed app publicly accessible

options.name: --slug
options.description: Public URL slug to use for publishing

options.name: --private
options.description: Require Automaton login to access the published app

options.name: --forkable
options.description: Allow other users to fork this published app

options.name: --open
options.description: Open the published app in the browser after success

options.name: --non-interactive
options.description: Disable prompts and rich terminal rendering
